summary: Grafton Elliot Smith worked in archaeology and history. He studied at Sydney Medical School, the University of Sydney, and St John's College, and later held a post at University College London from around 1919 to 1936.
Graham E. Clarke worked in Tibetology and other fields. He held positions at the Institute of Development Studies and at the University of Oxford, where he was attested as a Senior Member in 1998.
Graham Lock is a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

Graham Parkes is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. After earning his Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley, he served at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1979–2008) and University College Cork (2008–2013).

Graham Priest works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge, the London School of Economics under John Lane Bell, and Melbourne, he held posts at Melbourne, St Andrews, and the City University of New York Graduate Center.

Graves Chamney Haughton was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Fort William College. He co-founded and served as secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society and was a professor at the East India Company College (1819–1827).

Gray Tuttle is a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and history. He completed his Ph.D. at Harvard University in 2002 under Leonard van der Kuijp, William C. Kirby, and Philip A. Kuhn, and later held professorships at Columbia University.

Graziadio Isaia Ascoli was an Italian linguist and Indologist who founded the Archivio Glottologico Italiano in 1873. He served as a professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano from 1861 to 1902.

Greg Bailey is an Indologist who studied under J. Durham and Madeleine Biardeau, completing his PhD at the University of Melbourne. He was a visiting fellow at the University of Tübingen and served as a professor at La Trobe University.

Gregor Ahn is a religious studies scholar who studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit at the University of Bonn and the University of Copenhagen. He taught at the University of Münster and served as a professor at Heidelberg University from 1996 to 2025.

Gregory Adam Scott works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Columbia University, he has held academic posts attested in 2026 at the University of Edinburgh and the University of Manchester.

Gregory Forgues is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a master's degree at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher and also studied under Birgit Kellner as well as several traditional teachers.

Gregory Hillis is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed an MA at the University of Virginia in 1993 and later held posts at the University of Virginia and the University of California, Santa Barbara.

Gregory Max Seton works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Naropa University, UC Santa Barbara, and the University of Oxford, where he completed his D.Phil. under Vesna Wallace and Alexis Sanderson.
Gregory Nagy is a scholar of linguistics and related fields. He studied at Indiana University Bloomington and Harvard University before joining the faculty at Harvard University around 1969.

Gregory P. A. Levine is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University and later served as an associate professor of art history at the University of California, Berkeley.

Gregory Price Grieve specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at San Francisco State University and the University of Chicago, taught at DePaul University, and became professor and department head at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro.

Gregory Schopen is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the Australian National University. He held faculty posts at Indiana University Bloomington, Brown University, the University of Texas at Austin, and UCLA.

Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin was an Indologist and historian. He studied under George de Roerich at Moscow State University, where he later taught, alongside long-term posts at the Institute of Oriental Studies and the Russian Academy of Sciences.
Gritli von Mitterwallner was an Indologist and historian. She completed her doctorate and habilitation at the University of Munich, where she later served as a professor from 1978 to 1991.
